newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Telecom, ITJ outline merger terms.
newsitem.headline: Japan Telecom, ITJ outline merger terms.

text.p: Japan Telecom Co Ltd (JT) and International Telecom Japan Inc (ITJ) said on Tuesday that they would merge to form a new company and the merger ratio would be 12 ITJ shares for every JT share.
The merger, which is due to take effect on October 1, will strengthen the competitiveness of the companies in the fast-growing global telecom market, the two firms said in a statement.

"We are convinced that the new company will offer sufficient information and telecommunication services from a global viewpoint, and help develop the nation's telecommunications business," the company said. Japan Telecom president Koichi Sakata will head the merged company while ITJ is to dissolve upon the merger, they said.
As a result of the planned merger, the new company will issue 33,333.33 new shares with a face value of 50,000 yen each, the two firms said.

They forecast the new company will post a current profit of 41 billion yen in the year ending in March 1998, and 46 billion yen in the following business year. The new company's annual dividend is expected to be 6,000 yen per share for both 1997/98 and 1998/99.
